summary: Campbeltown Airport serves the Kintyre peninsula on the southwest coast of Scotland, providing a vital air link between this remote region and the central belt. The airport sits near the site of the former RAF Machrihanish, a long-standing military airfield that played roles in both World Wars. Today it operates as a small regional airport handling scheduled services primarily to Glasgow.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly from Campbeltown Airport?
A: Loganair operates scheduled passenger services from Campbeltown, primarily connecting to Glasgow Airport with a short flight across the Firth of Clyde.

Q: How far is the airport from Campbeltown town centre?
A: The airport is located approximately 3 miles (5 km) northwest of Campbeltown town, a short drive of around 10 minutes.

Q: Does the airport have international flights?
A: No, Campbeltown Airport only handles domestic flights within Scotland. There are no scheduled international services.

Q: Are there car rental facilities at the airport?
A: Car hire is limited; visitors are generally advised to arrange rental vehicles in advance or pre-book taxis from local operators in Campbeltown.
transport_tips: A taxi or pre-arranged car hire is the most practical option for reaching Campbeltown town from the airport, as public transport links are infrequent. The drive into town follows the A83 along the coast. Visitors should confirm return transport options before arriving, as taxi availability can be limited during off-peak hours.
local_tip: If you have time before your flight, visit the nearby Campbeltown Heritage Centre or take a short drive to the famous Machrihanish Beach, one of the longest and most scenic beaches in Scotland, just minutes from the airfield.
